text:
Minnesota arrives in Philadelphia with points in five straight (4-0-1), fresh off a 5-1 win at Washington where Kirill Kaprizov hit 500 career points and David Spacek picked up his first NHL point. The Wild are without Jared Spurgeon and both Foligno brothers. Philadelphia snapped a three-game winless run with a 6-3 win over Utah and is without Rasmus Ristolainen. Bobby Brink also makes his first trip back to Philadelphia since leaving the Flyers after 201 games.

The gap in how these teams play is wide. At five on five, MIN has taken 54% of the expected goals in its games (a measure of chance quality) and PHI only 40%. The Flyers also take 4.3 penalties a game, which keeps handing out power plays. In net, projected starter Jesper Wallstedt (MIN) is +10.9 in goals saved above expected this season, and Joseph Woll (PHI) is +3.6. Last year the pair read +5.8 and -7.4. Our model has MIN at 3.54 expected goals tonight and PHI at 2.55.

Kaprizov is our top scorer pick, at 53% to score and 81% for a point, and Matt Boldy sits at 44%. For Philadelphia, Matvei Michkov has 10 points in his last ten games, and PHLY Sports' Charlie O'Connor posted that he "is on fire, and just cannot be denied right now." Under the radar, we like Brink as a depth scorer: 2.4 expected goals in his last 10 games, with 17% to score and 39% for a point. He's a player to watch, not a lock.
